Discreet SOS, confidential reporting, hybrid AI, and area hotspots by case volume. GPS needs phone Location ON. Cloud sync needs login and network.

Sign in with an NGO_STAFF or NGO_ADMIN cloud account to load server aggregates and report flags. Local device preview remains available below.
Server aggregates use a minimum count threshold. Report flags show category, time, and urgency only — never another user’s private report text.

Some people at risk of GBV/FGM do not have a smartphone or internet. This phone app stays useful offline. A separate USSD channel is designed for feature phones — it is not running as a live nationwide service in this build.

Linda Binti on Android is not a USSD service. There is no live shortcode in this project. Safaricom (or any other operator) is not integrated unless a licensed USSD gateway is later connected to the Linda Binti backend.

Feature phone → licensed USSD gateway → Linda Binti backend → anonymous GBV/FGM report or safety request → authorized NGO dashboard. Emergency numbers 999, 112, 1195, and 116 already work from any phone.
What works on this smartphone without internet

Education, safety guidance, survivor support, risk questions, local report storage, trusted contacts, emergency guidance, and support-service numbers are saved on this phone. Optional cloud sync waits until internet, consent, and a USER account are available.

SOS still uses ordinary SMS to your trusted contacts. It needs SEND_SMS permission, a SIM, and airtime. It does not need internet and is not replaced by the backend. Location permission is optional and never blocks the SMS.

Android permissions: SEND_SMS for SOS; location only if you want a map link. Mobile network: SMS send/receive. Backend + internet: optional report sync, AI flags, stakeholder dashboard. Licensed USSD provider: any future feature-phone menu. No shortcode is published here.
